title: Signer-first policy and tool mutation CLI/MCP surfaces
intent: Policy and tool approval semantic mutation surfaces publish signed Nostr events first, verify relay OK acceptance, and expose follow metadata instead of mutating repositories or services directly.
observed_behavior_before: The CLI policy create command used the REST policy client mutation path rather than the operator signer/control-plane publisher.
MCP policy create, update, delete, and evaluate tools invoked PolicyService mutation/evaluation methods directly.
MCP tool provisioning approve/reject tools mutated ToolProvisioningRepository intent state and approval logs directly.
Read-only policy list/get and tool provisioning status paths legitimately used durable read models, but the semantic mutation distinction was not documented for users or MCP clients.
intended_behavior: PolicyCreate, PolicyUpdate, PolicyDelete, and PolicyEvaluate mutation surfaces publish signed public Nostr events of kinds 5986, 5987, 5988, and 5989 respectively.
Tool provisioning approval/rejection mutation surfaces publish signed ToolApprovalResponse events of kind 7977.
Publishers verify relay OK acceptance by requiring at least one accepted relay and propagate relay rejection/no-acceptance failures to the caller.
CLI and MCP mutation responses return follow metadata for canonical observables rather than claiming direct durable completion from request submission.
Read-only list/get/status paths may continue to read durable projections, and denylist administration remains documented as a distinct admin path rather than a tool approval semantic mutation.
scope: cmd/cli policy create signer-first operator path
internal/controlplane policy command publisher direct event semantics
non_goals: Deployment and artifact CLI/MCP mutation surfaces are intentionally out of scope because bahia-hygp owns that concurrent work.
Policy list/get and tool provisioning status read-model queries are not converted to mutation publishers.
Tool denylist administration is not redefined as ToolApprovalResponse semantics in this slice.
